records.source: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.
records.gloss: Men brothers and fathers, hear of me the to you now defense.
pieces: "Brothers and fathers, listen now to the defense I am making before you."

L.1: "Men, brothers and fathers, hear my defense [which I make] to you now."

R.1: "My brothers, and you respected older men, please listen to me. I want to answer the charges against me."

decisions.choice: men, brothers and fathers: a formal, respectful address to the Jewish crowd
alternatives: the men of the crowd only
decisions.reason: Stephen opens his speech before the council with the same words (7:2). Here Paul speaks to the crowd that had run together in the temple courts from the whole city (21:30-36), which need not have been men only. "Brothers" claims kinship with them as fellow Jews. Whether the address takes in the women present cannot be settled from the words.

decisions.choice: fathers: the older, respected men among the hearers
decisions.reason: Living hearers are addressed, as in 7:2, so the word is a title of respect for elders, not a reference to ancestors.

decisions.choice: defense: a reply to charges, as in a court
decisions.reason: The word is used of a legal defense (25:16; 2 Timothy 4:16). The crowd had accused Paul of teaching against the people, the law and the temple (21:28). He answers by telling his own story.

decisions.choice: brothers and fathers, with no inclusive setting; Literal keeps "men, brothers and fathers"
decisions.reason: "Brothers and fathers" is a set pair of address, as in 7:2. An inclusive form of the first word alone would read oddly beside "fathers", so the pair is kept as spoken; the meaning note says that women may have been among the hearers.

decisions.choice: you respected older men; I want to answer the charges against me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title "fathers" and the word "defense" mean here.

records.heading: Paul's defense to the people of Jerusalem

records.source: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν.
records.gloss: Having heard but that in the Hebrew language he was addressing them, more they gave quiet.
pieces: When they heard him speaking to them in Hebrew, they grew even quieter.

L.2: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they became all the more quiet.

R.2: The people heard that Paul was speaking to them in Hebrew, their own language. So they became even more quiet.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew language: the language of the Jews of the land, most likely Aramaic, possibly Hebrew itself
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 21:40 and 26:14. In the first century the everyday speech of Jews in Judea was Aramaic, and John uses the related word for Aramaic place names (John 5:2; 19:13). Hebrew was also still in use, so either is possible.

decisions.choice: even more quiet: the hush of 21:40 deepened
alternatives: they kept quiet instead of shouting
decisions.reason: There was already a great silence when he began (21:40). Hearing their own language rather than Greek, they listened even more closely.

decisions.choice: Hebrew, their own language
decisions.reason: Readable says why the language mattered to the crowd.

records.source: καὶ φησίν·
records.gloss: And he says:
pieces: Then he went on:

decisions.choice: says: a present tense in a past story, making the scene vivid
decisions.reason: Greek storytellers sometimes switch to the present tense at a turning point. The speech that follows is the past event being told.

decisions.choice: went on; said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the whole story in the past tense; Literal shows the Greek present. Readable names Paul.

records.source: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ, πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον, ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρ’ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.
records.gloss: I am a man a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, brought up but in the city this at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to [the] strictness of the ancestral law, a zealot being of the God even as all you are today, \v 4 who this the Way persecuted as far as death, binding and handing over to prisons men both and women, \v 5 as also the high priest bears witness to me and all the council of elders; from whom also letters having received to the brothers to Damascus I was going to bring also those there being bound to Jerusalem in order that they might be punished.
pieces: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia but raised here in this city. I sat at the feet of Gamaliel and was trained with great precision in our ancestral law. I was as zealous for God as every one of you is today.
I persecuted this Way to the point of death, putting men and women alike in chains and handing them over to prison.

The high priest himself can confirm this, and so can the whole council of elders. I even got letters from them to our fellow Jews in Damascus, and I set off to bring the people there back to Jerusalem in chains to be punished.

L.3: "I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the strictness of the ancestral law, being zealous for God, just as all of you are today,
L.4: who persecuted this Way to [the] death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women,
L.5: as the high priest also bears me witness, and all the council of elders. From them I also received letters to the brothers, and I was going to Damascus to bring those who were there also to Jerusalem in chains, so that they might be punished.

R.3: "I am a Jew. I was born in the city of Tarsus, in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem. I studied under Gamaliel, the teacher of the law. He taught me to keep every detail of the law handed down from our ancestors. I was eager to serve God, just as all of you are today.
R.4: I fought against the people who followed this Way, so hard that some of them died. I arrested men and women and put them in prison.
R.5: The high priest and all the council of elders can tell you that this is true. They gave me letters to our fellow Jews in Damascus. So I went there to arrest the believers and bring them back to Jerusalem in chains to be punished.

decisions.choice: at the feet of Gamaliel: as his pupil
decisions.reason: Pupils sat before their teacher, so to sit at someone's feet meant to learn from him (Luke 10:39). Gamaliel was a Pharisee and teacher of the law honored by all the people (5:34).

decisions.choice: at the feet of Gamaliel: goes with "brought up", and the training follows from it
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after the name, so the phrase ends the clause about his upbringing in Jerusalem. Either way, Paul's training under Gamaliel is meant.

decisions.choice: strictness: exact, careful keeping of the law
decisions.reason: The word means exactness. Paul calls the Pharisees "the strictest party of our religion" (26:5).

decisions.choice: zealous for God: wholly devoted to God and his law
alternatives: a member of the Zealot party
decisions.reason: The word is used of devotion to the law in 21:20 and of Paul's earlier life in Galatians 1:14. It does not name the later rebel party here.

decisions.choice: the Way: a name for the followers of Jesus and their teaching
decisions.reason: Luke uses the name in 9:2, 19:9, 19:23, 24:14 and 24:22.

decisions.choice: to the point of death: his persecution went as far as killing
alternatives: until he himself was near death
decisions.reason: Paul says in 26:10 that he cast his vote against believers when they were put to death, and 22:20 recalls Stephen. The phrase does not say how many died.

decisions.choice: council of elders: the Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same word for the council that tried Jesus (Luke 22:66).

decisions.choice: the high priest bears me witness: the high priest can confirm it
alternatives: the high priest is present now as a witness
decisions.reason: The present tense appeals to the office and its records. The high priest who gave Saul his letters (9:1) need not be the one now in office (23:2).

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow Jews in Damascus, not believers
decisions.reason: The letters were to the synagogues (9:2). Paul calls his Jewish hearers "brothers" in the same way (22:1; 28:17).

decisions.choice: our fellow Jews
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the brothers were, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: here in Jerusalem; Gamaliel, the teacher of the law; the believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the city, says who Gamaliel was, and says who "those there" were.

decisions.choice: I fought against the people who followed this Way, so hard that some of them died
alternatives: I persecuted this Way to the death
decisions.reason: Readable says what persecuting "to the death" meant, as the meaning note explains. It keeps the number of deaths unstated.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ, ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
records.gloss: It happened but to me journeying and drawing near to Damascus about noon suddenly out of the heaven to flash a light great around me, \v 7 I fell and to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why me do you persecute?
pieces: As I was traveling and coming close to Damascus, at about midday, all at once a brilliant light from heaven blazed around me.
I dropped to the ground and heard a voice say to me, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'

L.6: And it happened to me, as I was journeying and drawing near to Damascus, about noon, [that] suddenly a great light out of heaven flashed around me.
L.7: And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'

R.6: I was on my way, and I was getting close to Damascus. It was about noon. Suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed all around me.
R.7: I fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice speaking to me. It said, 'Saul, Saul, why are you attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'

decisions.choice: about noon: in full daylight
decisions.reason: The detail is not in 9:3. At midday the sun is at its brightest, yet the light was brighter still (26:13).

decisions.choice: great: very strong, intense
decisions.reason: The word means enough or considerable; with "light" it means a strong, bright light.

decisions.choice: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me: the same words as in 9:4 and 26:14
decisions.reason: Each telling of the event keeps these words. The doubled name is a solemn call, as when God calls "Abraham, Abraham" (Genesis 22:11).

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for what Saul was doing to the believers.

records.heading: A light from heaven near Damascus

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην· Τίς εἶ, κύριε;
records.gloss: I then answered, Who are you, Lord?
pieces: 'Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?' I answered.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address to the heavenly speaker, whom Saul does not yet know
alternatives: the full confession of Jesus as Lord
decisions.reason: Saul does not know who is speaking, so the word may be only a respectful title. But he has seen a light from heaven, and Luke's readers know who the Lord is. The same question comes in 9:5 and 26:15.

records.source: εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.
records.gloss: He said and to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene whom you persecute.
pieces: He told me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting.'

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.'

R.8: He said to me, 'I am Jesus from Nazareth. I am the one you are attacking.'

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: from Nazareth, the name by which Jesus was known
decisions.reason: Peter uses the same name in 2:22 and 3:6. This telling adds it; 9:5 has only "I am Jesus".

decisions.choice: whom you are persecuting: to persecute Jesus's followers is to persecute him
alternatives: Saul had persecuted Jesus in person
decisions.reason: Saul had attacked the believers (22:4), not Jesus himself. The risen Lord counts what is done to his people as done to him.

decisions.choice: of Nazareth; from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the name means.

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: As in 22:7.

records.source: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.
records.gloss: Those but with me being the indeed light beheld the but voice not heard of the one speaking to me.
pieces: My companions saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the one who was speaking to me.

L.9: Now those who were with me saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me.

R.9: The people traveling with me saw the light. But they did not hear the voice of the one who was talking to me.

decisions.choice: did not hear the voice: the companions did not hear the words spoken to Saul
alternatives: they heard no sound at all
they heard a sound but did not understand it
decisions.reason: In 9:7 the men traveling with Saul stood speechless, "hearing the voice but seeing no one". Here they "saw the light" but "did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me". In 9:7 the word "voice" is in the genitive case after the verb; here it is in the accusative. Some take the difference to mean they heard a sound but did not hear it as words, since the verb can mean to hear with understanding (1 Corinthians 14:2). Others take the two accounts as differing in detail. The case difference does not settle it, since in 22:7 Paul "heard a voice" with the genitive and understood it. Both accounts agree that only Saul received the message.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "saw the light"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("saw indeed the light, and were afraid"), add these words. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: my companions; the people traveling with me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who they were in fewer words.

records.source: εἶπον δέ· Τί ποιήσω, κύριε;
records.gloss: I said then, What shall I do, Lord?
pieces: I asked, 'What should I do, Lord?'

L.10: And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?'

R.10: I asked, 'Lord, what should I do?'

decisions.choice: what shall I do: a question that offers obedience
decisions.reason: The form asks what he ought to do. Saul now places himself under the Lord who has spoken to him.

records.source: ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν πρός με· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.
records.gloss: The and Lord said to me, Having risen go into Damascus, and there to you it will be told about all things which it has been appointed to you to do.
pieces: The Lord answered, 'Get up and go on into Damascus. There you will be told all that has been assigned for you to do.'

L.10: And the Lord said to me, 'Get up [and] go into Damascus, and there you will be told about everything that has been appointed for you to do.'

R.10: The Lord told me, 'Get up and go into Damascus. Someone there will tell you everything God has planned for you to do.'

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, who has just named himself
decisions.reason: The speaker is the one who said "I am Jesus" (22:8).

decisions.choice: it will be told; it has been appointed: God is the one who appoints, and someone will tell him
decisions.reason: The passives leave the agents unnamed. The appointing is God's (22:14), and Ananias is the one who tells him (22:12-16).

decisions.choice: someone there will tell you; God has planned
alternatives: it will be told you; it has been appointed
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
records.gloss: As but not I was seeing from the glory of the light that, being led by the hand by those being with me I came into Damascus.
pieces: Because the glory of that light had left me unable to see, my companions led me by the hand, and I came into Damascus.

L.11: And since I could not see because of the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me and came into Damascus.

R.11: That light was so bright and full of glory that I could not see. So the people with me led me by the hand into Damascus.

decisions.choice: glory: shining splendor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the bright splendor of God's presence (Luke 2:9; Acts 7:55). Here it is the brilliance of the light that blinded him.

decisions.choice: I could not see: a lasting blindness
decisions.reason: The tense describes a state. He was blind for three days (9:9).

decisions.choice: so bright and full of glory
decisions.reason: Readable says what the glory of the light was.

records.source: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων, ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον· κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Ananias then a certain, a man devout according to the law, borne witness to by all the dwelling [there] Jews, \v 13 having come to me and having stood by said to me, Saul brother, see again; and I in the very hour looked up at him.
pieces: There was a man named Ananias, devout in keeping the law and well regarded by all the Jews who lived there.
He came and stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' In that very moment my sight came back, and I looked up at him.

L.12: And a certain Ananias, a man devout according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living [there],
L.13: came to me, and standing by [me] said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight.' And at that very hour I looked up at him.

R.12: In Damascus there was a man named Ananias. He was a man who honored God and obeyed the law. All the Jews who lived there spoke well of him.
R.13: He came and stood next to me. He said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' Right then I could see again, and I looked at him.

decisions.choice: devout according to the law: careful to keep God's law
decisions.reason: The word describes reverent, careful people (2:5; 8:2). "According to the law" says how his devotion showed.

decisions.choice: Paul describes Ananias as his hearers would value him: a law-keeping Jew respected by the Jews of Damascus
alternatives: a different Ananias from the one in Acts 9
decisions.reason: In 9:10 Luke calls Ananias a disciple. Speaking to a crowd that accuses him of attacking the law (21:28), Paul stresses that the man who received him was faithful to it. Both descriptions hold.

decisions.choice: receive your sight; I looked up: the same verb, meaning both "see again" and "look up"
decisions.reason: Ananias tells him to see again, and in that hour Saul "looked up" at him: his sight returned, and his first sight was Ananias.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow Jew and now a fellow believer
decisions.reason: Ananias greets Saul as one of his own (9:17).

decisions.choice: see again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words; the last clause says both that his sight came back and that he looked at Ananias.

decisions.choice: in Damascus
decisions.reason: Readable says where Ananias lived.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.
records.gloss: He and said, The God of the fathers of us appointed you to know the will of him and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice out of the mouth of him, \v 15 for you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
pieces: Then he said, 'The God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} has chosen you beforehand to know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear words from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own mouth.
You will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witness to everyone, telling what you have seen and heard.

L.14: And he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth,
L.15: for you will be a witness for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to all {{gender:people|men}} of what you have seen and heard.

R.14: Then he said, 'The God our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worshiped has chosen you. He chose you to know what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants. He chose you to see Jesus, the Righteous One, and to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} speak to you.
R.15: You will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witness to all people. You will tell them what you have seen and heard.

decisions.choice: has appointed: chosen in advance for a task
decisions.reason: The verb means to choose or appoint beforehand (3:20; 26:16).

decisions.choice: our fathers: the forebears of Israel
decisions.reason: Ananias names the God of Israel's forebears, as Peter did in 3:13 and 5:30.

decisions.choice: the Righteous One: a title of Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter (3:14) and Stephen (7:52) use the same title. "His mouth" is the Righteous One's: Saul heard Jesus speak.

decisions.choice: witness: one who tells what he has seen and heard
decisions.reason: As in 1:8 and 26:16, a witness testifies about Jesus from what he knows firsthand.

decisions.choice: all people: all human beings, Gentiles as well as Jews
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead to 22:21, where the Lord sends Paul to the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Jesus, the Righteous One; He chose you
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and repeats the verb to keep the sentences short.

records.source: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις;
records.gloss: And now why do you delay?
pieces: Now why wait any longer?

L.16: And now why are you delaying?

decisions.choice: why are you delaying: there is no reason to wait
decisions.reason: The question urges him to act at once; Saul had not refused.

records.source: ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Having risen be baptized and wash away the sins of you, having called on the name of him.
pieces: Get up and be baptized. Let your sins be washed away as you call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.'

L.16: Get up, be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.'

R.16: Get up and be baptized. Have your sins washed away as you call on the name of the Lord Jesus.'

decisions.choice: be baptized; wash away: forms that mean "have yourself baptized" and "have your sins washed away"
alternatives: wash away your own sins by your own effort
decisions.reason: Both verbs are in the middle voice: Saul submits to what is done for him. The cleansing is God's work, received as he calls on the Lord.

decisions.choice: baptism, the washing away of sins and calling on his name belong together
alternatives: baptism only follows a forgiveness already complete
decisions.reason: Peter joins baptism with forgiveness in 2:38, and "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" in 2:21 (Joel 2:32). The sentence ties the washing to baptism and to calling on the name, without saying which brings about forgiveness.

decisions.choice: his name: the name of the Righteous One, Jesus
decisions.reason: The nearest "he" is the Righteous One (22:14). Believers are those who call on Jesus's name (9:14, 9:21).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "his name"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the name of the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("calling on the name of the Lord"), have "the Lord". Others, some of them early, have "his". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the one called on, as the meaning note explains. The pronoun could also be read as God.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι· Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: It happened then to me having returned to Jerusalem and praying of me in the temple to come me into a trance \v 18 and to see him saying to me, Hurry and go out in speed out of Jerusalem, because not they will receive your testimony about me.
pieces: After I had come back to Jerusalem, I was praying in the temple when I fell into a trance.
I saw the Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem at once, for the people here will not accept what you tell them about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.17: And it happened to me, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance
L.18: and saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying to me, 'Hurry and go out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.17: Later I went back to Jerusalem. One day I was praying in the temple, and I fell into a trance.
R.18: I saw the Lord Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem right away. The people here will not accept what you say about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: trance: a state in which a person sees a vision
decisions.reason: Peter falls into the same state in 10:10 and 11:5.

decisions.choice: a loosely built sentence
decisions.reason: The sentence refers to Paul first with one case, then another, then a third. The meaning is plain.

decisions.choice: praying in the temple: Paul shows his reverence for the temple
decisions.reason: The crowd had accused him of defiling the temple (21:28). This visit is likely his first return after Damascus (9:26-30; Galatians 1:18).

decisions.choice: him: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: The one he sees speaks of testimony "about me", and Paul answers "Lord" (22:19).

decisions.choice: the Lord; the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Paul saw, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: A trance in the temple

records.source: κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·
records.gloss: And I said, Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating in each the synagogues those believing on you;
pieces: I answered, 'Lord, these people know well what I did. In one synagogue after another I had those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} locked up and beaten.

L.19: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating, in synagogue after synagogue, those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}};

R.19: I answered, 'Lord, these people know what I used to do. I went into the synagogues and found those who believed in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I put them in prison and had them beaten.

decisions.choice: Paul's reply: since they know what he once did, his change should persuade them
alternatives: he pleads that he is unworthy
decisions.reason: Paul seems to argue that the people of Jerusalem, who knew him as a persecutor, would have to take note of his turn. The Lord answers by sending him away all the same (22:21).

decisions.choice: beating in the synagogues: punishment by the synagogue authorities
decisions.reason: Synagogues could punish members by flogging (Matthew 10:17). Paul later received such floggings himself (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: those who believe in you: those who trust in Jesus
alternatives: those who agree with his teaching
decisions.reason: The phrase names the believers by their trust in the Lord, as in 9:42 and 11:17.

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.
records.gloss: and when was being poured out the blood of Stephen the witness of you, also I myself was standing by and approving and guarding the garments of those killing him.
pieces: When Stephen, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness, was put to death and his blood poured out, I was there myself. I agreed with what they did, and I looked after the cloaks of those who killed him.'

L.20: and when the blood of Stephen, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness, was being shed, I myself was also standing by and approving, and guarding the garments of those who were killing him.'

R.20: Stephen was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness. When they killed him, I was there. I agreed that they should kill him. I even took care of the coats of the men who were killing him.'

decisions.choice: witness: one who testified about Jesus, here a witness whose testimony ended in his death
alternatives: martyr, in the later sense of one who dies for the faith
decisions.reason: The word means a witness, as in 1:8 and 22:15. Stephen bore witness to Jesus before the council and was killed for it. The later sense "martyr" grew out of passages like this one and Revelation 2:13, but here the word still means witness.

decisions.choice: Stephen's death: the events of 7:58-8:1
decisions.reason: The witnesses laid their cloaks at Saul's feet (7:58), and Saul approved of the killing (8:1, the same verb as here).

decisions.choice: his blood was poured out: he was violently killed
decisions.reason: Shedding blood means killing (Luke 11:50; Romans 3:15).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "approving"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("consenting unto his death"), add these words, likely from 8:1. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: witness
decisions.reason: The English word "martyr" carries the later sense, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: four short sentences, beginning with Stephen
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence into steps.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.
records.gloss: And he said to me, Go, for I to Gentiles far away will send out you.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, 'Go! I am going to send you far away, to the Gentiles.'"

L.21: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Go, for I will send you out far away to [the] Gentiles.'"

R.21: But the Lord said to me, 'Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles, the people who are not Jews.'"

decisions.choice: Gentiles: the peoples who are not Jews
decisions.reason: The word sets the Gentiles against the Jews of Jerusalem who will not accept his testimony (22:18). It is the word that ends his hearing (22:22).

decisions.choice: send out: commission and send, as an apostle
decisions.reason: The verb is built on the same root as "apostle". The commission matches 26:17.

decisions.choice: I: the emphatic "I" of the Lord himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis: it is the Lord who sends him.

decisions.choice: the Lord; the people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says who the Gentiles are.

records.source: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες· Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον, οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
records.gloss: They were listening then to him until this the word, and they lifted up the voice of them saying, Away from the earth such a one, not for it was fitting him to live.
pieces: The crowd heard him out until he said this. Then they raised a shout: "Take a man like this off the face of the earth! He should never have been allowed to live!"

L.22: And they listened to him until this word, and they raised their voices, saying, "Away with such a [man] from the earth, for it was not fitting [for] him to live!"

R.22: The people listened to Paul until he said this. Then they started shouting, "Kill him! Get rid of him! A man like this should not be allowed to live!"

decisions.choice: until this word: until he spoke of being sent to the Gentiles
alternatives: until the end of the speech
decisions.reason: The crowd accepted his story until the Lord sent him to the Gentiles (22:21). That seemed to confirm the charge that he taught against the people (21:28).

decisions.choice: away with such a man from the earth: a cry for his death
alternatives: send him out of the country
decisions.reason: The crowd had shouted "Away with him!" in 21:36, as the crowd shouted about Jesus (Luke 23:18).

decisions.choice: it was not fitting: he ought to have been dead already
decisions.reason: The past tense says it was never right for him to live.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: a past tense, "it was not fitting"
alternatives: many manuscripts have a present form, "it is not fitting"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a present participle with the same root. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Kill him!
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the crowd wanted, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: A Roman citizen by birth

records.source: κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα, ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Crying out and them and throwing off the garments and dust throwing into the air, \v 24 ordered the tribune to be brought him into the barracks, having said with whips to be examined him so that he might know for what reason thus they were shouting against him.
pieces: They kept yelling, flinging off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air.
So the tribune ordered Paul taken into the barracks. He gave orders for him to be questioned under the whip, to find out why the people were shouting at him so.

L.23: And as they were crying out and throwing off [their] cloaks and throwing dust into the air,
L.24: the tribune ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined with whips, so that he might find out for what reason they were shouting against him like this.

R.23: They kept shouting. They threw off their coats and threw dust into the air.
R.24: So the tribune, the Roman commander, ordered his soldiers to take Paul into the barracks. He told them to whip Paul and question him. He wanted to find out why the people were shouting at Paul like this.

decisions.choice: throwing off cloaks and throwing dust: signs of rage and horror
alternatives: a sign that they were about to stone him
decisions.reason: Throwing dust was a gesture of anger and contempt (2 Samuel 16:13). Those who stoned Stephen laid aside their cloaks (7:58), so some see a readiness to stone him; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: throwing off: tossing off or waving their cloaks
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw. It can mean to throw off a garment or to toss it about in the air.

decisions.choice: the tribune: the Roman officer in command of the cohort in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The title means a commander of a thousand. He led the Roman garrison in Jerusalem (21:31). His name was Claudius Lysias (23:26).

decisions.choice: the barracks: the soldiers' quarters in the Antonia fortress, beside the temple
alternatives: a military camp outside the city
decisions.reason: The fortress overlooked the temple courts, with steps leading down to them (21:35, 21:40).

decisions.choice: examined with whips: questioned under flogging
decisions.reason: Romans questioned slaves and non-citizens under the whip to force out the truth. The whip was made of leather straps, sometimes weighted with metal or bone.

decisions.choice: Paul; the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

decisions.choice: the Roman commander; his soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says who the tribune was and who carried out his order.

records.source: ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος· Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;
records.gloss: As but they stretched forward him with the straps, said to the standing by centurion the Paul, If a man a Roman and uncondemned it is lawful to you to flog?
pieces: They had stretched him out and tied him with straps when Paul said to the centurion on duty, "Does the law allow you to flog a Roman citizen, and one who has had no trial?"

L.25: But when they had stretched him out with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing [there], "Is it lawful for you to flog a man [who is] a Roman and uncondemned?"

R.25: The soldiers stretched Paul out and tied him with leather straps. Then Paul spoke to the centurion, the officer standing there. He asked, "Are you allowed to whip a Roman citizen? I have not even been found guilty!"

decisions.choice: they stretched him out with the straps: they tied him down with leather straps
alternatives: they stretched him out for the lashes of the whip
decisions.reason: The word for straps can mean the thongs that tied a prisoner or the thongs of the whip. Either way he was stretched out, ready to be flogged.

decisions.choice: Roman law forbade flogging a Roman citizen, above all without trial
decisions.reason: Roman laws protected citizens from being flogged, and from being punished without a trial. Paul raised the same point at Philippi (16:37).

decisions.choice: a Roman: a Roman citizen
alternatives: a man from the city of Rome
decisions.reason: In 16:37-38 and here the word means one who has Roman citizenship.

decisions.choice: uncondemned: not tried and found guilty
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 16:37.

decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: He served under the tribune.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "a Roman" means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: two sentences: a question and a protest
decisions.reason: Readable splits Paul's question in two.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων· Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν;
records.gloss: Having heard then the centurion having gone to the tribune reported saying, What are you about to do?
pieces: When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune and told him, "What is this you are about to do?

L.26: And when the centurion heard [this], he went to the tribune and reported [it], saying, "What are you about to do?

R.26: When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune. He said, "Do you know what you are about to do?

decisions.choice: what are you about to do: a warning in the form of a question
decisions.reason: The centurion warns his commander that he is about to break the law.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "What are you about to do?"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "See" or "Take care" before it
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("Take heed what thou doest"), add a word of warning. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Do you know what you are about to do?
alternatives: What are you about to do?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the warning in the question plain.

records.source: ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.
records.gloss: The for man this a Roman is.
pieces: This man is a Roman citizen!"

L.26: For this man is a Roman."

R.26: This man is a Roman citizen!"

decisions.choice: a Roman: a Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

records.source: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Λέγε μοι, σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ;
records.gloss: Having come near then the tribune said to him, Tell me, you a Roman are?
pieces: The tribune came over and asked him, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?"

L.27: And the tribune came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?"

R.27: So the tribune came to Paul and asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?"

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, with surprise
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: the tribune can hardly believe that this prisoner is a citizen.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ναί.
records.gloss: He and said, Yes.
pieces: "Yes," he said.

decisions.choice: he said, Yes: a plain answer
decisions.reason: The tense of the verb is a common one for reporting a reply.

decisions.choice: I am; Paul
decisions.reason: Readable completes the answer and names the speaker.

records.source: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος· Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην.
records.gloss: Answered then the tribune, I with a great sum the citizenship this acquired.
pieces: The tribune replied, "It cost me a great deal of money to get this citizenship."

L.28: And the tribune answered, "I acquired this citizenship for a large sum."

R.28: "I became a citizen only by paying a large amount of money," the tribune said.

decisions.choice: bought citizenship: citizenship obtained by payment
decisions.reason: Under the emperor Claudius citizenship could be obtained for money, often by bribes to officials, as the Roman historian Cassius Dio reports. The tribune's name, Claudius Lysias (23:26), fits a man who took the emperor's name when he became a citizen.

decisions.choice: a large sum: a great amount of money, not stated
decisions.reason: The word means a sum of money. No figure is given, so no modern value can be stated.

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, perhaps doubting that a man like Paul could be a citizen
decisions.reason: The tribune may be suggesting that citizenship is costly and that Paul does not look able to have bought it.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη· Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.
records.gloss: The but Paul was saying, I but even have been born [so].
pieces: Paul answered, "And I am one by birth."

L.28: But Paul said, "But I was even born [a citizen]."

R.28: Paul answered, "I have been a citizen since I was born."

decisions.choice: born a citizen: his father or an earlier forebear was a Roman citizen
decisions.reason: How Paul's family gained citizenship is not said. One born a citizen held a standing older than the tribune's.

decisions.choice: a citizen; one
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves "citizen" to be understood from the tribune's words.

records.source: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς.
records.gloss: Immediately therefore withdrew from him those being about him to examine; and the tribune also was afraid having learned that a Roman he is and that him he had bound.
pieces: At once the men who were going to question him backed away. The tribune, too, grew afraid once he learned that Paul was a Roman citizen, since he had had him tied up.

L.29: So those who were about to examine him immediately withdrew from him; and the tribune also was afraid, having learned that he was a Roman, and that he had bound him.

R.29: The men who were going to whip and question Paul quickly moved away from him. The tribune was afraid too. He had found out that Paul was a Roman citizen, and he had already had Paul tied up.

decisions.choice: had bound him: had him tied for flogging, or had him chained
decisions.reason: Paul had been chained since 21:33, and tied with straps for the whip (22:25). To bind a citizen for flogging without trial broke the law. He stays in custody (22:30; 23:10).

decisions.choice: the tribune was afraid: an officer who mistreated a citizen could be punished
decisions.reason: Roman law protected citizens, and an officer who broke it could answer for it.

decisions.choice: examine: question under the whip
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 22:24.

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Paul.

decisions.choice: whip and question
decisions.reason: Readable says what the examination was, as in 22:24.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.
records.gloss: On the then next day desiring to know the certain thing, why he is accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered to come together the chief priests and all the council, and having brought down the Paul he set [him] among them.
pieces: On the following day, since the tribune wanted to learn the true reason for the charges the Jews were bringing against Paul, he freed him from his chains. He summoned the chief priests and the full council, then brought Paul down and placed him in front of them.

L.30: And on the next day, wanting to know for certain why he was being accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the council to assemble, and he brought Paul down and set [him] before them.

R.30: The next day the tribune wanted to know for sure why the Jews were accusing Paul. So he took off Paul's chains. He ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet together. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand in front of them.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the high council of the Jewish people in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The council was led by the high priest, with chief priests, elders and scribes (4:5-6; 5:21). Paul once had letters from its members (22:5).

decisions.choice: released him: freed him from his chains, while keeping him in custody
decisions.reason: Paul is still the tribune's prisoner (23:10).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "released him"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("loosed him from his bands"), add these words. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: brought down: from the fortress down to where the council met
alternatives: took him to a lower court
decisions.reason: The Antonia fortress stood above the temple courts (21:35).

decisions.choice: the Jews: Paul's Jewish accusers
decisions.reason: The charges came from Jews from Asia and the crowd that followed them (21:27-28).

decisions.choice: the tribune; Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

decisions.choice: freed him from his chains; took off Paul's chains
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was released, as the meaning note explains.
